questions.q: Who actually executes the function when a model makes a tool call?
options: Your application's own code
The model itself, inside the API
Anthropic's infrastructure, always
No execution happens — it's just a suggestion
questions.explain: For client tools, the model only requests the call — your application runs the real function and reports the result back.

questions.q: What three fields define a tool in the tools array?
options: endpoint, method, headers
role, content, id
name, description, input_schema
model, max_tokens, messages
questions.explain: A tool definition is its name, a description the model uses to decide when to call it, and a JSON Schema (input_schema) for its arguments.

questions.q: What does the input field of a tool_use block contain?
options: A raw, unparsed JSON string you must decode yourself
An already-parsed object matching the tool's input_schema
The original user question
Nothing — input is only present in the request, not the response
questions.explain: input arrives as a parsed object matching your schema, ready to use directly — no manual JSON parsing needed.

questions.q: How do you send a tool's result back to the model?
options: As a system message update
By calling a separate /tool_result endpoint
As an assistant message containing the raw output
As a user message with a tool_result content block referencing the tool_use_id
questions.explain: The tool_result block goes in a new user message and references the exact tool_use_id the model's call carried.

questions.q: What does setting tool_choice to {"type": "any"} do?
options: Forces the model to call some tool, without specifying which one
Forces the model to never call a tool
Forces one specific named tool to be called
Lets the model decide freely, same as the default
questions.explain: "any" requires the model to call some tool from the array, as opposed to "tool" (a specific one), "none", or the default "auto".
